Red pandas are found in the Eastern Himalayas and mountainous forests of Asia [d1, d6]. Their range includes Nepal, India, Bhutan, Myanmar (Burma), and China [d4, d5, d7]. Within China, they are located in provinces such as Sichuan and Yunnan [d2]. They inhabit high-altitude, temperate forests with bamboo understories [d2, d7, d9]. The population is traditionally divided into two groups: the Himalayan red panda (found in Nepal, India, Bhutan, and southern Tibet) and the Chinese red panda (found in China and Myanmar) [d2, d3, d7].
